rw [← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg
      (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S (Localization.Away (f t))) (fun _ => rfl), hF t,
    ← hcw t]
  exact hU (ci t) (cj t) (cw t)

/-! ## The producer: `IsChartClause` is the whole remaining debt -/

include hO hchi in
/-- **A `DivRepAffinePullback` from `IsChartClause` alone** — the point of this file.

`DivRepAffinePullback.ofPull` asks for three fields; all three are now available from the
single per-chart ε clause:

* `pull` is `divRepPullValue`, whose conditionality on `IsCompatible` is discharged by
  `IsChartClause.isCompatible`;
* `isDivRepClassify_pull` is `isDivRepClassify_divRepPullValue`;
* `pull_naturality` is `divRepPullValue_naturality` (ε-free);

and `pull_classify` is derived by the separation theorem.  Composing with
`DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy` (`Picard/DivRepGlobalClassify.lean`) this turns the
DDR9-U ε-identity into the *only* remaining input of divisor representability. -/
noncomputable def divRepAffinePullback_ofChartClause
    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
    (hU : DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U) :
    DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 :=
  DivRepAffinePullback.ofPull hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
    (fun S _ _ => divRepPullValue hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 U
      (DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause.isCompatible hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 hU) S)
    (fun S _ _ v =>
      isDivRepClassify_divRepPullValue hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 U hU S v)
    (fun phi v => divRepPullValue_naturality hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 U
      (DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause.isCompatible hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 hU) phi v)

include hO hchi in
/-- **Divisor representability from the ε-identity**: `divFunctor C π g` is represented by
`divSchemeOver` as soon as some chart family satisfies the per-chart clause.

This is the DDR-9 endpoint with its remaining hypothesis made explicit and singular.  Read
the honest form: nothing here *proves* U2, and per roadmap `…divrep.u2` the clause is still
gated on the G-4 certificate discharge.  What is now true is that a producer of U2 needs to
supply nothing else. -/
noncomputable def divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartClause
    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
    (hU : DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U) :
    (divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver :=
  DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi)
    (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2)
    (divRepAffinePullback_ofChartClause hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 U hU)

include hO hchi in
/-- **Divisor representability from U2 exactly as the worksheet states it** — the form a
producer should quote.

`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.1 states U2 at the *identity point* of each chart
(`S = R_Z`, `ω = id`), and `IsChartClause.of_id` shows the `ω`-quantifier of the interface
adds nothing.  So the whole divisor-representability chain rests on: *for each pair chart,
the supplied chart class is classified by that chart's own morphism to `DivScheme`*.

Nothing below the endpoint is left to do.  What is left is that statement, which is U2, and
which is gated on the G-4 certificate discharge. -/
noncomputable def divFunctor_representableBy_of_id
    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
    (hid : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (U i j) (ChartMap i j)) :
    (divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver :=
  divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartClause hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 U
    (DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause.of_id hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 hid)

end Clause

AJC's Cluster D' (the Milne-Kollar replacement for Quot) rests on
`Scheme.DivFamily`. On 2026-07-29 I measured: 135 mention sites, **zero producers** —
no declaration anywhere returns one, no `Nonempty`, no `.mk` application, no
empty-divisor constructor. Every site consumes an assumed `x : DivFamily π T`.

**Why:** this is invisible to the vacuity sweeps this workspace runs. Those look for
the `HasDivFunctor` shape (a class field that fails to mention its object) and for
`choose_spec`-of-own-binder. `DivFamily` passes both: it is a plain structure whose
six fields correctly mention the curve and the family. Nothing is false. But every
theorem quantifying over it is about no divisor, which is the `HasPicScheme` defect
one layer below where the audits look — at a structure rather than a class.

**How to apply:** when pricing a cluster, ask "what inhabits the carrier?" separately
from "is the statement about the right object?". A correct statement over an
uninhabited structure is worth less than its sorry-count suggests. Note the
interaction: if a route's tail turns out *false* (p1 landed
`not_representableBy_picSharp_of_not_isIso_picEtComparison`), then building the
producer converts vacuous-but-true statements into wrong ones — so re-aim before
inhabiting. Related: [[gap-count-vs-gap-cost]],
[[price-the-consumer-carrier]], [[subsingleton-not-finrank-for-vanishing]].

AJCR, 2026-07-29 (run 0089 r3): human protection I-0492 replaced the chart-typed divisor
carrier with the widened `DivFamZarAff`. Predecessors built it well — quotient carrier, base
change, functoriality, gluing keystone, functor `divFunctorAff`, comparison `divFunctorToAff`,
a Picard **class** `picClass` with naturalities. Zero declarations carried it to
`PicEtAff`/`picEt`/`relPic`/`pic0`; the whole Abel layer sat at the old carrier. The consumer
that needs representability (`abelSigmaChart`) binds the **old** functor. So policy mandated
one carrier and the consumer bound another, joined by nothing.

**Why:** sorry counts, axiom probes and vacuity sweeps are per-declaration; rootedness is
per-module. None asks whether a path exists from a carrier to the category a consumer's
signature names. A missing *arrow* between two individually-correct layers is invisible to all
of them.

**How to apply:** when a decision replaces a carrier, census declarations whose *statement*
mentions the source carrier **and** the target namespace, as a pair, case-insensitively
(producers sit in suffix position — [[case-sensitive-grep-misses-producers]]). Then read the
consumer's signature for which carrier it binds. The repair was a verbatim transcription (10
declarations, no new mathematics), so this mode is cheap to fix and expensive to detect — the
arrows out of a replaced carrier are the work item nobody opens a row for. Relatedly, I priced
the residue as *obstructed* by reading which names a cited proof mentions rather than what that
step outputs; see [[read-what-the-step-outputs]] and [[reprice-the-prescription-before-paying-it]].

## 7.6 The gate is L8, not U2 — and that is the round's main finding

Inbox **I-0365**. The framing "the divrep tail is independent of the certificate; the certificate
gates U2" is false, but not in the direction the tree assumed.

`DivFamZar` is **by definition** a quotient of *locally certified* families
(`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:224` the setoid, `:235` the def, `:71` `IsLocallyCertified` — note it
localises on the base only). So certificates are **free on the consuming side**:
`DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover` (`Picard/DivRepClassifyZarKit.lean:433`) is a landed theorem,
unfolded by every classifier keystone (`DivRepClassifyZar.lean:128/:176/:230`,
`DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean:361/:363`), and `IsDivRepClassify` (`DivRepClassifyZar.lean:90`)
quantifies over certified families as a *hypothesis*, so their scarcity makes it easier, not harder.

The bite is on the other side. The no-go (`DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:123` — clause (c1) *is*
leak-freeness — and `:131`) says `DivFamZar` is blind to connected divisors meeting both pinned
fibres. So `divFunctor C π g` is a **proper subfunctor** of degree-`g` relative divisors.
Representing it is not the problem; the L9–L13 tail does that honestly. The problem is that a
too-small divisor functor **cannot cover Pic⁰**: the Abel map out of it is not Zariski-locally
surjective, because the classes whose only witnesses are the invisible divisors are never hit.

One nuance that sharpens where to look: the no-go's hypothesis is `IsPreconnected d.supportLocus`,
and **over a field it is vacuous** — the support of a divisor is a finite set of closed points, so
preconnected forces a single point, which cannot meet two disjoint fibres. The blindness is a
purely *relative* phenomenon: a family over a positive-dimensional base whose total support is a
connected horizontal curve sweeping from `π⁻¹(0)` to `π⁻¹(∞)` is invisible, and base shrinking does
not help because every neighbourhood of the crossing contains points on both sides. So
Riemann–Roch-level, fibrewise coverage is untouched — but local surjectivity of a *presheaf* map is
tested on arbitrary scheme tests, which is exactly the relative direction.

**Consequences.** (i) Stop calling U2 or the affine package "the gate": they are tail work and are
nearly finished. (ii) Do not attack L8 against `divFunctor` as it stands — it is arguably false,
not merely hard. (iii) Judge R1 and R2 by whether they widen `DivFamZar` enough for L8, not by
whether they make a certificate easier to prove. A third widening is worth costing beside them:
replace `IsLocallyCertified` outright by the standard relative effective Cartier divisor (finite
locally free of rank `g` over the base), which carries no chart-adaptation artifact at all.

§7.1 was written to correct §1 for trusting a `MISSING` claim across an integrate commit. Its
own L11 row has now aged the same way, in one day, and by the same mechanism.

**§7.1 said:** "What is left of L11 is the general-test **classifier** and the two inverse
laws." **Truth at HEAD:** all three landed on 2026-07-27, in commits `31930badb` and
`aeb77e174`, as `Picard/DivRepGlobalClassify.lean` — `classifyGlobal` (`:204`),
`pullGlobal_classifyGlobal` (`:252`), `classifyGlobal_pullGlobal` (`:269`), plus
`toGlobalData` (`:288`) and the endpoint `DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy` (`:306`).

obligations**, and the divisor-representability endpoint L9 is reachable from a single
structure.

**The chain below L9 is therefore one object, not five.** Everything from L10 to L13 collapses
to: produce a term of `DivRepAffinePullback` (`Picard/DivRepAffKit.lean:175`). By
`DivRepAffinePullback.ofPull` (`Picard/DivRepAffPullbackReduce.lean:140`) that is three fields.

**What this run landed, and one gating claim it retracts.** The roadmap leaf `…divrep.u2` and
`w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.4 both describe the affine package as "U2 + choice bookkeeping",
which reads as though the bookkeeping sat behind the ε-identity. It does not:

* `Picard/DivRepAwaySpanGlue.lean` — the eight-field instance pack of the S5b gluing keystone
  `DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat`, discharged at the canonical away carriers
  `Localization.Away (f p)` / `Localization.Away (f p * f q)`. This pack was the mechanical
  obstruction between the atlas factorization (which returns a *bare* spanning family) and
  every gluing keystone (which wants carriers as instance data).
* `Picard/DivRepAffPullGlue.lean` — the chart pulls of one factorization glue, uniquely.
* `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` — `divRepPullGlue_eq_of_chartFactors`: two *different*
  factorizations of the same morphism give the same class. **U2-free.**

The reason the last one is free is a property of a landed lemma nobody had used:
`divRepPullAt_mapAlgHom_eq_of_chartFactor` (`Picard/DivRepAffChartOverlap.lean:126`) compares
**any two chart presentations of the same morphism**, over any two carriers, restricted to any
common tower ring — it never asks that they share a factorization. So the cross-refinement of
two factorizations is handled by the very lemma that handles one factorization's own overlaps.

**What genuinely remains ε-gated**, and it is a smaller target than "U2 + bookkeeping":
`isDivRepClassify_pull` (the glued pulled class satisfies the characterizing clause) and
`DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible` for the universal family — which by
`isCompatible_of_isDivRepClassify_divRepPullAt` is itself the per-chart clause, i.e. U2.
`pull_naturality` is still unwritten but is the same glue machinery as `pull`; its carrier
transport is landed (`Picard/DivRepAwayPush.lean`).

"U2-free" is a claim about the *proof*, not about the gate. `DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible`
has no producer, and its only intended producer is U2. So nothing above lets a consumer
actually instantiate the new theorems without proving U2 first: the set of unproved statements
is unchanged. What changed is its **partition** — factorization-independence is no longer a
second obligation standing beside U2 — and therefore the size of the remaining target. Read
the round's result as "the tail is one structure with two ε-gated fields", not as "a gate
cleared". The general form of this trap is inbox `I-0512`.

**Also landed but not yet consumed by anything**: the `pull` field itself is still not
*defined*. The ingredients are all here (`divScheme_exists_chartFactor` gives the
factorization, `exists_divRepPullGlue` glues it, `divRepPullGlue_eq_of_chartFactors` makes the
result choice-free), and assembling them is a `Classical.choice` over the factorization
characterized by the restriction property. That is the concrete next step and it is small.

**§7.6's finding stands and is unaffected.** L8 (local surjectivity of the Abel map out of a
too-small divisor functor) remains the campaign's real gate; nothing above touches it. What
changed is only that the *tail* below L9 is now one structure with one ε-gated field, so the
cost of the tail is no longer a reason to defer confronting L8.

15	# U2's ε-identity at the universal point, from the certificate alone
16	
17	The DDR9-U ε-identity (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.1 U2) asks that the
18	tautological pair-chart data at the universal point satisfy the ε-identity: over the
19	`Z(♦)`-chart ring `R_Z`, the certified family of the universal seed has
20	
21	> `ε = (x₁, x₂)`  with  `x₁ = divUniversalFstWindow`, `x₂ = divUniversalSndWindow`
22	
23	the universal tautological pair.  This file discharges that identity from **one**
24	hypothesis, `IsCertified`, having found that the other three inputs of the landed
25	ε-projection identity are already available at the universal point.
26	
27	## What was already landed, and had not been composed
28	
29	`ThetaGeneratorSeed.divFamEps_certifiedFamily` (`Picard/DivSchemeEps.lean`) takes four
30	inputs beyond the seed: a generator clause `hD`, a certificate `hc`, two `thetaGluedEval`
31	surjectivities, and the second-window containment `hle₂`.  At the universal point:
32	
33	* **`hD` is free** — `PointwiseAchiever.isGenerator_highWindowPointwiseGeneratorSeed`
34	  (`Picard/DivSchemeHighWindowPointwiseGenerator.lean`) is a generator clause for the
35	  seed at `K = divUniversalSeedK`, over `R_Z` itself, from `hO`, `hχ` and
36	  `hb : 0 < windowBound π hπ` only.  It routes through `pointwiseSeedRDN_of_highWindow`,
37	  so it needs **no** germ-divisibility input: it is *not* `isGenerator_seedUniv'`, which
38	  is the seed whose RD-N hypothesis is the recorded geometric wall (I-0302 §residual
39	  2b/2c).  Two different seeds over the same ring, and only one of them is gated.
40	* **`hle₂` is free** — `PointwiseAchiever.divUniversalSndWindow_le_highWindow_divisorWindow`
41	  (`Picard/DivSchemeHighWindowSecondContainment.lean`) is exactly the second-window
42	  containment *for this seed*, from the same three hypotheses.
43	* **both surjectivities are free given `hc`** —
44	  `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified.thetaGluedEval_surjective`
45	  (`Picard/DivisorThetaFibreData.lean`) derives them from the certificate itself, at any
46	  window `≥ M` with the ledger `H¹` input.  The second window is `M + s ≥ M`.
47	
48	So the ε-identity at the universal point is a **corollary of the certificate**, and the
49	composition is what this file records.  Nothing here is new mathematics; what is new is
50	that the four inputs are the *same* seed's, which is why the composite had not been
51	formed — the generator and containment lemmas live in the 44-file `DivSchemeHighWindow*`
52	family, which is sorry-free but was **not reachable from the root aggregator**, so no
53	root-target measurement ever saw them (the failure mode of inbox `I-0362`, at
54	44-file scale, on the critical path).
55	
56	## Main declarations
57	
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseAchiever.divFamEps_highWindow_eq_universal_pair` — **the
59	  DDR9-U ε-identity at the universal point**: `ε` of the certified family of the
60	  high-window universal seed is the universal tautological pair.  One hypothesis beyond
61	  the ambient ledger data: the certificate.
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseAchiever.exists_certifiedFamily_divFamEps_eq_universal_pair`
63	  — the existential form, which is what a chart-class producer consumes.
64

68	`IsCertified` input is the standing G-4 obligation and is the widened certificate lane's

70	unproved.  What changes is that its ε-identity half is no longer an obligation at all —
71	the debt is exactly a certificate at the universal point, with `0 < windowBound π hπ`
72	as a scalar side condition.
73	-/

/-- **A `DivRepAffinePullback` from `IsChartClause` alone** — the point of this file.

`DivRepAffinePullback.ofPull` asks for three fields; all three are now available from the
single per-chart ε clause:

* `pull` is `divRepPullValue`, whose conditionality on `IsCompatible` is discharged by

* `isDivRepClassify_pull` is `isDivRepClassify_divRepPullValue`;
* `pull_naturality` is `divRepPullValue_naturality` (ε-free);

and `pull_classify` is derived by the separation theorem.  Composing with
`DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy` (`Picard/DivRepGlobalClassify.lean`) this turns the
DDR9-U ε-identity into the *only* remaining input of divisor representability. -/

    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
    (hU : DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U) :

This is the DDR-9 endpoint with its remaining hypothesis made explicit and singular.  Read

/-- **Divisor representability from U2 exactly as the worksheet states it** — the form a
producer should quote.

/-- The general-test equivalence underlying the represented functor. -/
noncomputable def equiv
    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
    (T ⟶ DivOver) ≃ divFamZar C pi g T where
  toFun := D.pull
  invFun := D.classify
  left_inv := D.classify_pull
  right_inv := D.pull_classify

set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
@[simp]
theorem equiv_apply
    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver) :
    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D T v
      = D.pull v :=
  rfl

set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
@[simp]
theorem equiv_symm_apply
    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) :
    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D T).symm F
      = D.classify F :=
  rfl

/-- The final F7 categorical packaging: natural general-test pullback equivalences
represent the locally certified divisor functor by `DivScheme`. -/
noncomputable def representableBy
    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2) :
    (divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver where
  homEquiv {T} :=
    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D T
  homEquiv_comp {T T'} f v := by
    change D.pull (f ≫ v) = divFamZar.map C pi g f (D.pull v)
    exact D.pull_comp f v

set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
@[simp]
theorem representableBy_homEquiv_apply
    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver) :
    (representableBy (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1)
      (b2 := b2) D).homEquiv v = D.pull v :=
  rfl

set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
@[simp]
theorem representableBy_homEquiv_symm_apply
    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) :
    (representableBy (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1)
      (b2 := b2) D).homEquiv.symm F = D.classify F :=
  rfl

end DivRepGlobalData

11	# Locally certified divisor families: the `DivFamZar` carrier (DD-2 stage S5b)
12	
13	The Addendum-2 repair of the divisor-functor carrier (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`,
14	Addendum 2): the globally-certified `DivFam` is not a Zariski sheaf — the diagonal
15	divisor over `Γ(C \ pt)` is certifiable on a basic-open cover of the base but carries
16	no global certificate — so the faithful functor value is the **locally certified**
17	quotient `DivFamZar`. The generic germ-regularity engines live in
18	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarKit`.
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyCertified` — the Addendum-2 frozen pin: a span-⊤ family
21	  `g : Fin m → R` with certified divisor families over `Localization.Away (g i)`
22	  divisor-equal to the pulled system; `hreg` is discharged by the Kit's open-immersion
23	  lemma, with the S4 instance provided by `haveI`.
24	* `IsLocallyCertified.of_divEq` — the pin respects divisor equality.
25	* `CertifiedDivisorFamily.isLocallyCertified` — a global certificate is a local one
26	  (trivial cover `g = ![1]`; the certified part is `mapAlg` to `Localization.Away 1`,
27	  whose equations ARE the pulled system on the nose).
28	* `IsLocallyCertified.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors` — **the mapAlg-hreg
29	  engine**: a locally certified system has regular pulled equations along the
30	  comparison of an ARBITRARY test tower `R → R'` — regularity is germ-local, each germ
31	  sits over a chart `Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))` of `R'`, where the
32	  local certificate's regularity transports through its `DivEq` and the landed
33	  certificate-based pullback regularity.
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar` — the quotient of locally certified systems by
35	  `DivEq`, with `mk`, `mk_eq_mk_iff`, `picClass`, and `DivFam.toZar`.
36	
37	Total `DivFamZar.mapAlg` and the Zariski keystones are
38	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarMapAlg` / `…ZarGlue`.
39	-/

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffPullNat
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepGlobalClassify

/-!
# F5 — `isDivRepClassify_pull` from the per-chart clause, and the whole package from U2

`Picard/DivRepAffPullField.lean` defines `pull` and `Picard/DivRepAffPullNat.lean` proves
`pull_naturality`.  The third field of `DivRepAffinePullback.ofPull` is
`isDivRepClassify_pull`, and this file discharges it — **from the same hypothesis
`IsCompatible` already needs**:

> `IsChartClause U` : for every chart `(i, j)` and every `ω : R_Z(i,j) →ₐ[k] S`, the chart
> pull `divRepPullAt U i j ω` satisfies `IsDivRepClassify` for the chart morphism
> `Spec ω ≫ ChartMap i j`.

That is precisely the hypothesis `isCompatible_of_isDivRepClassify_divRepPullAt`
(`Picard/DivRepAffPullbackReduce.lean`) consumes, i.e. the DDR9-U ε-identity in clause
form.  So the two obligations the round-5 framing listed side by side —
`isDivRepClassify_pull` **and** `IsCompatible` — are **one** obligation, and this file
proves that:

* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause` — the named U2 interface.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isDivRepClassify_divRepPullValue` — **the third field**: the glued
  pulled class satisfies the characterizing clause for the morphism it came from.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.divRepAffinePullback_ofChartClause` — **a producer of
  `DivRepAffinePullback` from `IsChartClause` alone**, hence (with
  `DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy`) of the divisor-representability endpoint.

**Why the clause is local on the base, which is the whole content.** `IsDivRepClassify F₀ v`
quantifies over tower tests `T` carrying a certified representative of `F₀`'s restriction
and a chart framing of its ε pair, and concludes an equality of morphisms out of `Spec T`.
Both the hypothesis data and the conclusion restrict along `T → T ⊗ …`; and a chart framing
over `T` together with the atlas factorization over the spanning family `f` gives, on each
`Localization.Away (f t)`-overlap, two chart presentations of the same morphism.  The
already-landed `pullback_chart_divClassifyClause_compat` is exactly that comparison, so the
`Scheme.Cover.hom_ext` chase is the same one `exists_isDivRepClassify` runs — this file
runs it against the *pulled* class rather than a classified one.

**What this does NOT do.** It produces no `IsChartClause`.  U2 — the ε-identity at the
universal point — is still unproved, and per the roadmap leaf it is gated on the G-4
certificate discharge (`ThetaGeneratorSeed.certifiedFamily` wants a global `IsCertified`
over the chart ring).  What changes is the *shape* of the remaining debt: a producer of the
divisor-representability endpoint now owes exactly one statement, stated in one place, with
no cover bookkeeping left around it.
-/

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance
8	
9	/-!
10	# C9b: `IsChartUniv` reduced to one clause about the chart locus
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` splits `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` into the two
13	clauses mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative` actually conjoins, and gives a criterion whose
14	input is elementwise.  This file instantiates that criterion at the Abel chart and at
15	`V := chartLocus`, which is the pair `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
16	
17	The point is to make the residue **one named clause about the chart locus** instead of the
18	whole certificate.  Concretely, the criterion's `ChartFibrePresented` datum has four fields,
19	and at the Abel chart three of them are supplied here:
20	
21	| field | at the Abel chart | status |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `W` | `chartLocus` of the test point's class, as an open | **shape supplied here**, but at the
24	  cost of `haff` — see the retraction below |
25	| `r` | the divisor family over the locus | the classifier `divRepClassifyZar` |
26	| `sq` | its class is the test's class | the classifier's own characterisation |
27	| `exists_factor` | uniqueness of the normalized representative | **the relative form of GAP-2** |
28	
29	So `W` needs only B-4 (**not** "nothing" — retracted below), `sq` is a property of whatever
30	`r` is, and the genuine content is
31	concentrated in `r` (a construction, from the classifier) and `exists_factor` (relative
32	GAP-2).  This file makes that split machine-checkable: `IsChartLocusFibre` below names
33	exactly the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple **at the chart locus**, and
34	`isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` proves `IsChartUniv` from it.
35	
36	## Why this is not a restatement
37	
38	A reduction that merely renames its obligation is worthless, and this one is checked against
39	that failure mode in two directions:
40	
41	* `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised, so the `W` field is a *shape* a lane
42	  no longer has to invent.
43	
44	  **RETRACTED 2026-07-29, second clause only** (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  This
45	  read "the `W` field costs zero, which is a real reduction of the datum from four fields to
46	  three".  The cost is not zero: `chartLocusOpens` takes the argument `haff`, and **nothing in
47	  the tree discharges it**.  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` removed the
48	  `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis but passes `haff` straight through, as does
49	  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it; the affine case that would feed it
50	  (`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`) is itself conditional on
51	  `IsChartDatumPresentation`, which is dat-b row B-4's named residue and is only half landed.
52	  So the datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  The
53	  residue is now named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4's own obligation by
54	  `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`;
55	* `isChartLocusFibre_of_isChartUniv` is the **converse**: `IsChartUniv` at the chart locus
56	  gives injectivity on every test, so a lane cannot obtain `IsChartUniv` while avoiding the
57	  content of `exists_factor`.  The reduction is therefore an equivalence in the direction
58	  that matters, not a weakening.
59	
60	## Main declarations
61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens` — `chartLocus` as an honest `T.Opens`, using the
63	  unconditional general-test openness.  This is the `V` that `restrictChart` wants.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartLocusFibre` — the residue: the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple
65	  of the criterion, at the chart locus, for every test point.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` — **the reduction**: that triple
67	  gives `IsChartUniv` (hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)` pair) at any open.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isChartUniv` — the converse-direction check.
69	-/
70	
71	set_option autoImplicit false
72	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
73	
74	universe u
75	
76	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
77	
78	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
79	
80	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
81	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
82	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
83	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
84	
85	noncomputable section
86	
87	/-! ## The chart locus as an open of the test
88	
89	`chartLocus` is a `Set T.left` and `restrictChart` wants a `T.Opens`.  The bridge is the
90	openness theorem.  **"which is now unconditional — so this costs a hypothesis-free definition
91	rather than a gate" is RETRACTED** (2026-07-29): the general-test openness theorem is
92	unconditional in `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` but still takes the affine-local `haff`, which
93	nothing discharges.  See `chartLocusOpens`' docstring and
94	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`. -/
95	
96	variable (C) in
97	/-- **`chartLocus` as an open subscheme of the test.**
98	
99	For a test `T` presented as `Over.mk a` and a class `lam` on it, the chart locus is open by
100	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (CHART-U(b) at a general test, unconditional since
101	`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged), so it is an honest element of `T.Opens`.
102	
103	**THE `haff` SENTENCE HERE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED** (2026-07-29,
104	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  It read: "The `haff` hypothesis is the affine-local
105	input of that theorem and is *not* a residue of this file: it is what the landed affine
106	openness supplies."  The landed affine openness does **not** supply it.
107	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`) is conditional
108	on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — dat-b row B-4's own named residue, whose *witness* half is now
109	discharged too (`hconv`, by plus-unit injectivity,
110	`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`), leaving a plus-class base-change
111	identity — and no theorem in the tree produces `haff` for a general test.  It is a genuine
112	open obligation, named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4 by
113	`chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`.  It is
114	carried as an argument here so the definition does not silently depend on a chosen route. -/
115	def chartLocusOpens (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
116	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
117	    (haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
118	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))) :
119	    T.left.Opens where
120	  carrier := chartLocus C m Z lam
121	  is_open' := isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal' C m Z T lam haff
122	
123	@[simp]
124	lemma mem_chartLocusOpens {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
125	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T}
126	    {haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
127	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))}
128	    {t : T.left} :
129	    t ∈ chartLocusOpens C m Z T lam haff ↔ t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
130	  Iff.rfl
131	
132	/-! ## The residue, named -/
133	
134	variable (C π n) in
135	/-- **The residue of C9b, named**: for every test point of the Σ-sheaf, the chart point over
136	its chart locus together with the two properties the criterion needs.
137	
138	**THE NEXT SENTENCE WAS FALSE AND IS RETRACTED (2026-07-29,
139	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean`).**  It read: "This is `ChartFibrePresented` with its
140	`W` field already discharged — it is `chartLocus`, open unconditionally".  The `W` field is
141	**free**: it is a field of the structure, quantified inside the `Nonempty` below, and
142	`chartLocus` occurs nowhere in this definition — nor does `chartLocus` or `V` enter the proof
143	of `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre`.  The criterion consumes the datum for the
144	**unrestricted** chart, so this statement implies
145	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` at `V = ⊤`, hence `Mono`, hence injectivity on
146	every test — which `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` and
147	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214` all cite as FALSE for the Abel chart (its fibres
148	are the linear systems `|D|`).  If those headers are right this definition is
149	**unsatisfiable** and `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre`, though sorry-free, can never fire.
150	See `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective` for the guard instantiated here, and inbox
151	`I-0874`.  A lane must decide that fork before attacking `exists_factor`.
152	
153	Modulo that retraction, what a lane owes is:
154	
155	* `r`: the divisor family over the locus whose class is the given one.  This is the
156	  classifier `divRepClassifyZar` applied to the canonical-section family, i.e. CHART-U(c)'s
157	  construction;
158	* `sq`: that its chart value *is* the given class, which is the classifier's characterising
159	  property;
160	* `exists_factor`: that two points with the same class agree, i.e. the **relative form of
161	  DAT-C GAP-2** (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` in families).
162	
163	Stated as a `Prop` over an arbitrary presenting datum rather than as a structure carrying the
164	family, because the family is the classifier's output and this lane must not guess its shape:
165	the existential is over morphisms of schemes only. -/
166	def IsChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
167	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
168	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
169	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) : Prop :=
170	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
171	    Nonempty (ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) g)
172	
173	/-- **THE REDUCTION**: the residue above gives `IsChartUniv`, hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)`
174	pair, at *any* open of the divisor scheme.
175	
176	Two things are worth reading off the proof.  First, it goes through the criterion of
177	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` and then through the *composition* half
178	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` already landed in `Pic0ChartPair.lean` — so the two
179	halves of C9b compose exactly as the file headers predicted, with no seam.  Second, the open
180	`V` is arbitrary: restriction never has to be to the chart locus for `hf` to hold, because
181	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is stable under precomposition with an open immersion.  The chart
182	locus is where the *unrestricted* statement becomes true, which is a statement about
183	`IsChartLocusFibre`, not about `V`. -/
184	theorem isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
185	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
186	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
187	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
188	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
189	    (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg) (V : D.left.Opens) :
190	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
191	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V
192	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some)
193	
194	/-! ## The converse check: the reduction is not a weakening -/
195	
196	/-- **`IsChartUniv` forces elementwise injectivity of the restricted chart.**
197	
198	The converse direction of the reduction, and the reason it is a reduction rather than a
199	restatement: a lane that obtains `IsChartUniv` has, for free, the injectivity statement that
200	`ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor` is the hard half of.  So there is no route to `hf` that
201	avoids relative GAP-2 — the gate is real, and this file has moved it rather than removed it.
202	
203	Compare `isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective`: that says the criterion cannot
204	be *satisfied* without injectivity; this says the goal cannot be *reached* without it. -/
205	theorem injective_of_isChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
206	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
207	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
208	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
209	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
210	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
211	    Function.Injective ((restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V).app T) :=
212	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf h T
213	
214	end
215	
216	end AlgebraicGeometry

33	## What is proved, and what is assumed
34	
35	The straddling geometric input is **assumed**, exactly as protection `I-0492` clause 2 directs
36	(USE Stacks `0B8B`, do not re-derive it) — so the theorems below are conditional on the same
37	one input the whole lane is conditional on, and on nothing else.  What they add is that this
38	single input suffices to *separate* the two carriers: no second hypothesis appears on the
39	chart-typed side, because the refutation needs none.
40	
41	The separation is **field-independent**: no hypothesis on `|P¹(k)|` occurs anywhere in either
42	half, which is why R2 and not a field-size hypothesis was the human's answer (`I-0492`).

44	## SCOPE — the joint inhabitation is NOT exhibited in Lean, and that is deliberate
45	
46	Read this before quoting the separation as "the widening is strict, proved".  The separation
47	below is a **conditional**: given a divisor satisfying both the straddling witnesses and the
48	`0B8B` containment, the two carriers disagree.  Whether such a divisor exists *in this Lean
49	tree* is a different question, and the honest answer is that no witness is constructed here:

51	* Mathematically the witness exists over **every** field, including `F₂` — `spec-dd-r.md`
52	  ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 builds it as `(g−1)Q₀ + Q₁` inside the universal divisor on `Sym^g C`, with no
53	  rational-point and no `k = k̄` hypothesis.
54	* Formalising it is explicitly **out of scope** by ADDENDUM 4 §4.5: it needs `Sym^g C` (or
55	  `Hilb^g`) with its universal flat divisor, mathlib has no symmetric products of schemes and no
56	  Hilbert or Picard schemes, and this tree constructs no curve other than `P¹`.

58	So per trap (c) of the axiom-probe catalogue (`I-0442`) these theorems are **not** certified
59	non-vacuous, and the predecessor's `n = 0` witnesses do not help: those inhabit the widened
60	endpoint's hypotheses at an EMPTY support locus, which directly contradicts `hx`/`hy` here.  A
61	straddling divisor has nonempty support by definition.  What the conditional does establish is
62	that the two carriers are separated *by one named geometric input and nothing else* — no second
63	hypothesis is smuggled in on the chart-typed side, because the refutation needs none.
64	
65	## WHY THE REFUTATION DOES NOT ALSO KILL THE WIDENED SIDE
66	
67	The two conjuncts below look close enough that a reader should be suspicious: both carriers get
68	per-piece swallow-or-miss from the *same* clopen-trace argument, which needs only that the piece
69	is **open** (`AffAdaptation.subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected_of_supportLeak`, the chart-free
70	twin of `DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:98`). So why is only the chart-typed side refuted?
71	
72	Because the chart-typed verdict is not the per-piece statement — it is an *upgrade* of it, and the
73	upgrade is where the pinned pair enters. `supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected` runs the
74	dichotomy at `V₀` and then uses **`relCover_sup`, i.e. `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`**, to conclude that a support
75	missing `V₀` lies in `V₁`. That step consumes the fact that there are exactly **two** charts
76	covering everything, so "misses this one" forces "inside that one".
77	
78	A widened `AffCoverData` has `m` pieces with `⨆ j, pieces j = ⊤` and no distinguished pair, so
79	missing one piece forces nothing — the support can sit inside a piece that is neither, which is
80	exactly what a straddling `W` from Stacks `0B8B` is. The widened layer therefore has swallow-or-miss
81	and **no** confinement verdict, and that asymmetry is the whole content of R2 rather than an
82	oversight. Grepping for a widened analogue of `supportLocus_subset_chart_*` returns nothing, and
83	the paragraph above is why nothing is missing.

180	  flat_sections_isAffineOpen C R (D.isAffineOpen j)
181	
182	/-- Piece overlaps are affine (the relative curve is separated over `Spec R`, being proper),
183	so the overlap section rings are flat too — the widened
184	`FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces_inf`. -/
185	theorem flat_sections_pieces_inf (i j : D.index)
186	    (hinf : IsAffineOpen (D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)) :
187	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) :=
188	  flat_sections_isAffineOpen C R hinf
189	
190	end AffCoverData
191	
192	/-! ## The optional chart typing, for the Θ-layer only -/
193	
194	/-- The pinned chart of a given side, spelled here so this file needs no import from the
195	Θ-layer (it agrees with `relPinnedChart` by `rfl`). -/
196	noncomputable def pinnedChartOfSide [IsAffineHom π] (b : Bool) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
197	  bif b then (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ else (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
198	
199	/-- **A chart typing of a widened cover**: an assignment of each piece to one of the two
200	pinned `P¹` charts, containing it.  This is what the Θ-twisting unit genuinely needs (the
201	theta cocycle lives on `V₀ ⊓ V₁`), and it is deliberately a SEPARATE datum: no certificate
202	clause and no locally-certified predicate may require it.  Keeping it separate is what stops
203	the old fixed-pair typing from being smuggled back in through a field. -/
204	structure ChartTyping [IsAffineHom π] (D : AffCoverData C R) where
205	  /-- Which pinned chart the piece is assigned to. -/
206	  side : D.index → Bool
207	  /-- The piece is contained in its assigned chart. -/
208	  piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ pinnedChartOfSide C R π (side j)
209	
210	/-! ## Migration: old cover data instantiates the widened datum -/
211	
212	namespace FinCoverData
213	
214	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)
215	
216	/-- **The migration map.** An old chart-typed `FinCoverData` gives a widened
217	`AffCoverData`: reindex `Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁` through `finSumFinEquiv`, the pieces are affine as
218	basic opens of the affine pinned charts, and the joint cover follows from the two chart-wise
219	covers together with `relCover_sup`.
220	
221	The point of this lemma is that widening costs nothing landed: every existing construction of
222	cover data still produces a legal widened datum.  The converse fails, and that is exactly the
223	content of R2. -/
224	noncomputable def toAffCoverData : AffCoverData C R where
225	  m := D.m₀ + D.m₁
226	  pieces := fun j => D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j)
227	  isAffineOpen := fun j => by
228	    rcases finSumFinEquiv.symm j with i | i
229	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inl]
230	      exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen _
231	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inr]
232	      exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen _
233	  cover := by
234	    refine top_le_iff.mp fun z _ => ?_
235	    -- every point is in a pinned chart, and each chart is covered by its own pieces
236	    have hz : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
237	        ⊔ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := by
238	      rw [relCover_sup]; trivial
239	    have key : ∃ i : D.index, z ∈ D.pieces i := by
240	      rcases Opens.mem_sup.mp hz with h | h
241	      · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (D.cover₀ h)
242	        exact ⟨Sum.inl i, hi⟩
243	      · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (D.cover₁ h)
244	        exact ⟨Sum.inr i, hi⟩
245	    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := key
246	    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨finSumFinEquiv i, by
247	      simpa only [Equiv.symm_apply_apply] using hi⟩
248	
249	@[simp]
250	lemma toAffCoverData_pieces (j : Fin (D.m₀ + D.m₁)) :
251	    D.toAffCoverData.pieces j = D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j) := rfl
252	
253	/-- The canonical chart typing of a migrated datum: chart-0 pieces are basic opens of `V₀`,
254	chart-1 pieces of `V₁`. -/
255	noncomputable def toChartTyping : ChartTyping C R π D.toAffCoverData where
256	  side := fun j => (finSumFinEquiv.symm j).isRight
257	  piece_le := fun j => by
258	    rw [toAffCoverData_pieces]
259	    rcases h : finSumFinEquiv.symm j with i | i
260	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inl]
261	      exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h₀ i)
262	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inr]
263	      exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h₁ i)
264	
265	end FinCoverData

267	end AlgebraicGeometry

namespace DivRepChartFamily

/-- **The DDR9-U interface in clause form** (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.1 U2, as
consumed rather than as stated): each chart pull of the supplied family satisfies the
backward classifier's characterizing clause for its own chart morphism.

This is *verbatim* the hypothesis `isCompatible_of_isDivRepClassify_divRepPullAt` takes, so
naming it costs nothing and buys the observation this file is for: the same statement also
gives `isDivRepClassify_pull`, hence the entire `DivRepAffinePullback`. -/
def IsChartClause
    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g) : Prop :=
  ∀ {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S),
    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2
      (divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega)
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j)

set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
-- The `letI` re-topologization of the tower test as a `ChartRing`-algebra makes the
-- elaborator unify TWO algebra structures on `T` (through `omega`, and the ambient
-- `k`/`S`-tower) while `divRepPullAt` unfolds `mapAlgHom`; same defeq profile as
-- `divRepPullAt_awayMul_compat`, well past the default budget.
set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
/-- **The `ω`-quantifier of `IsChartClause` adds no strength**: it suffices to have the
clause at the *identity point* of every chart, which is exactly U2 as the worksheet states
it (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.1: `S = R_Z`, `ω = id`, `w = divCarveChartMk`).

`IsDivRepClassify` already quantifies over all `k`/`S`-tower tests, so base-changing the
chart point is free: retopologize a tower test `T` over `S` as a `ChartRing`-algebra through
`ω`, and a certified representative of `divRepPullAt U i j ω` over `T` *is* one of `U i j`
over `T`, because `divRepPullAt` is `mapAlgHom ω` and `mapAlgHom_comp` collapses the two
restrictions.  The framing is untouched, and the conclusion transports because
`algebraMap (ChartRing i j) T` factors as `(algebraMap S T).comp ω`.

So a producer owes the identity-point statement only — the one `divUniversalFamily` is built
to satisfy, whose left-hand side is `divUniversalFst` definitionally
(`Picard/DivSchemeFamilyUniv.lean:72-79`).  Found by a fresh-context review of this file
(inbox `I-0561`), which correctly observed that the interface as written advertises a *larger*
debt than is owed.

Note the curve-properness/irreducibility instances are genuinely unused here: the collapse is
a base-change bookkeeping fact about the clause, with no curve geometry in it (the linter is
silenced rather than `omit`-ed, because the ambient curve instances of this section are
mutually referenced and cannot be dropped individually). -/
theorem IsChartClause.of_id
    {U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g}
    (hid : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (U i j) (ChartMap i j)) :
    IsChartClause (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U := by
  intro S _ _ i j omega T _ _ _ _ GT hGT i' j' w hw1 hw2
  -- read `T` as a `ChartRing i j`-algebra through `omega`
  letI algCT : Algebra (ChartRing i j) T :=
    ((IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S T).comp omega).toRingHom.toAlgebra
  haveI towkCT : IsScalarTower k (ChartRing i j) T :=
    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (RingHom.ext fun x => by
      rw [RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
      exact (((IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S T).comp omega).commutes x).symm)
  -- the same certified family represents the unpulled class over `T`
  have hGT' : (DivFam.mk GT).toZar = DivFamZar.mapAlg T g (U i j) := by
    rw [hGT, divRepPullAt, ← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg
        ((IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S T).comp omega) (fun _ => rfl) (U i j),
      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp omega (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S T) (U i j),
      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S T) (fun _ => rfl)]
  -- and the chart morphism composes: `algebraMap (ChartRing i j) T = (algebraMap S T) ∘ omega`
  have hfac : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S T))
        ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom)
      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (ChartRing i j) T)) := by
    rw [← Spec.map_comp]
    rfl
  have hmain := hid i j T GT hGT' i' j' w hw1 hw2
  rw [← Category.assoc] at hmain
  rw [← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc, hfac]
  exact hmain

include hO hchi in
/-- The clause interface gives the compatibility the `pull` field is conditional on:
this is `isCompatible_of_isDivRepClassify_divRepPullAt` under its new name. -/
theorem IsChartClause.isCompatible
    {U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g}
    (hU : IsChartClause (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U) :
    IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U :=
  isCompatible_of_isDivRepClassify_divRepPullAt hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 U
    (fun i j omega => hU i j omega)

end DivRepChartFamily

9	/-!
10	# F5 — `isDivRepClassify_pull` from the per-chart clause, and the whole package from U2
11	
12	`Picard/DivRepAffPullField.lean` defines `pull` and `Picard/DivRepAffPullNat.lean` proves
13	`pull_naturality`.  The third field of `DivRepAffinePullback.ofPull` is
14	`isDivRepClassify_pull`, and this file discharges it — **from the same hypothesis
15	`IsCompatible` already needs**:
16	
17	> `IsChartClause U` : for every chart `(i, j)` and every `ω : R_Z(i,j) →ₐ[k] S`, the chart
18	> pull `divRepPullAt U i j ω` satisfies `IsDivRepClassify` for the chart morphism
19	> `Spec ω ≫ ChartMap i j`.
20	
21	That is precisely the hypothesis `isCompatible_of_isDivRepClassify_divRepPullAt`
22	(`Picard/DivRepAffPullbackReduce.lean`) consumes, i.e. the DDR9-U ε-identity in clause
23	form.  So the two obligations the round-5 framing listed side by side —
24	`isDivRepClassify_pull` **and** `IsCompatible` — are **one** obligation, and this file
25	proves that:
26	
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause` — the named U2 interface.
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isDivRepClassify_divRepPullValue` — **the third field**: the glued
29	  pulled class satisfies the characterizing clause for the morphism it came from.
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divRepAffinePullback_ofChartClause` — **a producer of
31	  `DivRepAffinePullback` from `IsChartClause` alone**, hence (with
32	  `DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy`) of the divisor-representability endpoint.
33	
34	**Why the clause is local on the base, which is the whole content.** `IsDivRepClassify F₀ v`
35	quantifies over tower tests `T` carrying a certified representative of `F₀`'s restriction
36	and a chart framing of its ε pair, and concludes an equality of morphisms out of `Spec T`.
37	Both the hypothesis data and the conclusion restrict along `T → T ⊗ …`; and a chart framing
38	over `T` together with the atlas factorization over the spanning family `f` gives, on each
39	`Localization.Away (f t)`-overlap, two chart presentations of the same morphism.  The
40	already-landed `pullback_chart_divClassifyClause_compat` is exactly that comparison, so the
41	`Scheme.Cover.hom_ext` chase is the same one `exists_isDivRepClassify` runs — this file
42	runs it against the *pulled* class rather than a classified one.
43	
44	**What this does NOT do.** It produces no `IsChartClause`.  U2 — the ε-identity at the
45	universal point — is still unproved, and per the roadmap leaf it is gated on the G-4
46	certificate discharge (`ThetaGeneratorSeed.certifiedFamily` wants a global `IsCertified`
47	over the chart ring).  What changes is the *shape* of the remaining debt: a producer of the
48	divisor-representability endpoint now owes exactly one statement, stated in one place, with
49	no cover bookkeeping left around it.
50	-/

138

141	`ω`, and a certified representative of `divRepPullAt U i j ω` over `T` *is* one of `U i j`

168	      rw [RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
169	      exact (((IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S T).comp omega).commutes x).symm)
170	  -- the same certified family represents the unpulled class over `T`

172	    rw [hGT, divRepPullAt, ← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg
173	        ((IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S T).comp omega) (fun _ => rfl) (U i j),
174	      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp omega (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S T) (U i j),
175	      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S T) (fun _ => rfl)]

    (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F

    (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D f v

/-- **Divisor representability from range membership of the chart maps** — the form this
file exists to state.

`divRepClassifyZar` is injective on classes (`eq_of_isDivRepClassify`), so representability
of `divFunctor` is *equivalent* to the classifier being surjective at every affine test.
This says surjectivity at the **chart rings alone** suffices: if each chart map
`ChartMap i j` is the classifier of *some* locally certified class over its own chart ring
`R_Z(i,j)`, then `divFunctor C π g` is represented by `divSchemeOver`.

Nothing here produces such a class; per roadmap `…divrep.u2` that is the G-4 obligation.
The value is the shape of what is owed: a *preimage under a landed map*, at
`glueData`-many points, rather than a quantified submodule identity. -/
noncomputable def divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange
    (hrange : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      ∃ F : DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g,
        (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 (ChartRing i j) F).left
          = ChartMap i j) :
    (divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver :=
  divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartClause hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
    (fun i j => (hrange i j).choose)
    ((DivRepChartFamily.isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
      (fun i j => (hrange i j).choose)).mpr (fun i j => (hrange i j).choose_spec))

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarSheaf

/-!
# The divisor functor (DD-2 S6b)

The one-screen functor packaging of the locally certified divisor vehicle
(`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §6, spelling (A) of I-0222, co-signed by the DD-R lane):

* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFunctor`: `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`, with object values
  `divFamZar C π n T` and action `divFamZar.map` — the `picEtFunctor` house pattern.
  Type-valued: degree-`n` divisor families carry no group structure.

This is the functor `divRep` is stated against (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 8,
Addendum 1).  The sheaf halves are consumed as-is from
`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarSheaf` (`ext_of_le_cover` /
`existsUnique_glue_of_le_cover`), the pic0/01JJ precedent.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161), so the pinned synthesis
depth must be set in-file for the faithful per-file check. -/
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π] (n : ℕ)

/-- **The divisor functor** (DD-2 S6b, the pinned name): the locally certified
degree-`n` divisor families as a presheaf of types on the slice over `Spec k`,
with the glued restriction `divFamZar.map` along arbitrary test morphisms — the
`picDegLayerFunctor` house pattern. -/
noncomputable def divFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u where
  obj T := divFamZar C π n T.unop
  map g := ↾divFamZar.map C π n g.unop
  map_id T := by
    ext s U
    exact congrArg (fun z : divFamZar C π n T.unop => z.1 U) (divFamZar.map_id C π n s)
  map_comp {T T' T''} g h := by
    ext s U
    exact congrArg (fun z : divFamZar C π n T''.unop => z.1 U)
      (divFamZar.map_comp C π n g.unop h.unop s)

@[simp]
lemma divFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
    (divFunctor C π n).obj T = divFamZar C π n T.unop :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma divFunctor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
    (s : divFamZar C π n T.unop) :
    (divFunctor C π n).map g s = divFamZar.map C π n g.unop s :=
  rfl

end AlgebraicGeometry

20	/-!
21	# U2's class half: the no-go DOES reach the Zariski-local pin, and its input narrows
22	
23	`Picard/DivRepChartClassUnivAny.lean:223-231` carries a warning that the roadmap leaf
24	`…divrep.u2` and three inbox items have since quoted as the leaf's price:
25	
26	> the hypothesis `HasCertifiedAdaptation` is **refuted** by
27	> `forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling` … So this theorem is a sound *reduction* whose
28	> hypothesis may be false; do not read it as "U2 is one certificate away".
29	
30	The warning is correct, and **it does reach the Zariski-local pin as well** — but only in a
31	NARROWED form, and the narrowing is what this file records.
32	
33	## What the no-go does and does not need
34	
35	*A first draft of this file claimed the no-go could not reach the pin, on the grounds that no
36	lemma carries `¬ IsLocallyCertified` and that the only landed implication runs
37	`isLocallyCertified_of_isCertified`, i.e. refuted-side → pin.  Both halves of that are true and
38	the conclusion drawn from them was wrong; the correction is kept in place of the claim because
39	the reasoning is the reusable part.*
40	
41	No bridge lemma is needed, because `forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling`
42	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffStrict.lean:127`) takes its base ring as a **section variable** and
43	its system as an implicit.  It therefore instantiates directly at
44	`R := Localization.Away r` with the **pulled** system, which is exactly the binder
45	`IsLocallyCertified` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:71`) uses.  A no-go stated over section
46	variables is a *schema*, not a statement about one ring, and "the pin quantifies over a
47	different ring" buys nothing against it.
48	
49	What the away form *does* buy is a strictly smaller refuting input.  To kill the pin one now
50	needs the two straddling witnesses **inside a single fibre** — the existential picks `r` with
51	`r ∉ p`, so witnesses lying over `p` survive whichever `r` is offered, but witnesses at
52	unrelated primes can be shrunk away.  Global straddling refutes
53	`HasCertifiedAdaptation`; only one-fibre straddling refutes the pin.  Two sibling headers state
54	this in prose already (`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:32`,
55	`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarVerdict.lean:25`: no Zariski shrink separates the witnesses).
56	
57	## What this file lands
58	
59	The per-prime route already in the tree
60	(`ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation`,
61	`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean:162`) produces the pin from away-localized
62	certificates.  This file instantiates it at the high-window universal seed, so that U2's
63	class half is stated at the binder a producer can actually target, and names the refuting
64	input that binder still admits.
65	
66	## Main declarations
67	
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseAchiever.ForallPrimeAwayCertified` — the away form of the
69	  class obligation, stated so that the ring each adaptation lives over is visible.
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseAchiever.divFamZarUnivOfForallPrimeAway` — the `DivFamZar`
71	  class at the universal point from it, with no certificate over `R_Z` in the input.
72	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_isCertified_not_conversely`
73	  — the direction record: the refuted side implies the pin.  Kept, with its name's `_not_
74	  conversely` read as a statement about the *implication*, not as a claim that the no-go
75	  fails to reach the pin — it does reach it, by instantiation at the away ring.
76	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.side_straddle_gives_chart_separated_pieces` — the
77	  probe's correct shape: opposite `side` values already separate the charts, so what is
78	  measurable is the `side` function, not a support locus.
79	
80	## What this does NOT do, stated exactly
81	
82	It produces **no certificate**, at no prime, so **no gate clears** and `rep` remains
83	undischarged.  It does not make the class half easier; it makes the *refuting* input harder,
84	which is a smaller and less exciting claim than the one this file's first draft made.
85	
86	**The away hypothesis has no witness at any prime**, here or anywhere in the tree, and it is
87	refutable exactly when the universal seed's support straddles within one fibre.
88	
89	**THE PROBE THIS SEAM STILL OWES, in the shape that is worth running.**  Nothing in the tree
90	compares `univSeed`'s support to the pinned charts, and the leaf is unpriced in both directions
91	until something does — two rounds have argued about whether a refutation reaches its target
92	instead of checking whether its antecedent holds.  But "does `univSeed` straddle?" is the wrong
93	spelling, and `side_straddle_gives_chart_separated_pieces` below says why:
94	
95	* every seed **piece** is confined to one pinned chart *by construction* — `piece_le` is
96	  `basicOpen_le` at `relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)`, so this is a fact about the *type*
97	  `ThetaGeneratorSeed` and there is nothing seed-specific to measure;
98	* but `localEquations` builds a **pointed** cover, one member per point, with `side` a function
99	  *of the point*.  So the support locus may straddle both charts globally while every piece is
100	  chart-confined.  Those are different statements.
101	
102	The measurement is therefore about the `side` **function**, not about a support computation:
103	*do two points of the support take opposite sides?*  That is where a lane should spend the
104	round.  (Established by `review-ajcr`, inbox `I-1003`; re-derived here rather than taken on
105	report, and the transport is the theorem below.)
106	
107	**Neither direction is settled by any of this, and the asymmetry is easy to mis-quote.**
108	Per-piece chart-confinement together with a `side` *function* **permits** global straddling; it
109	does not **produce** it.  So "the seed is chart-confined" must not be read as "it straddles",
110	and equally must not be read as "it cannot" — the first is what a producer needs ruled out, the
111	second is what a producer would need proved, and this file supplies neither.
112	
113	**One further thing unmeasured here, and it may be decisive** (`review-ajcr`, `I-1003`):
114	`ThetaGeneratorSeed` types its pieces *into* the pinned charts, which is the shape protection
115	`I-0492` clause 3 names as what made the earlier cheaper option vacuous.  If U2's class half
116	routes through the seed at all, it is on the **chart-typed** side of the widening by
117	construction, and the away-localization argument above inherits that confinement.  Were that so,
118	the retraction at the top of this file would have a *structural* cause rather than a proof-level
119	one.  Not measured here; worth testing before another round is spent on the away route.
120	
121	**Do NOT read the pinned-chart geometry as an obstruction.**  The certificate assemblers
122	(`DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`, `Picard/DivSchemeCertUniv.lean:104`)
123	consume a *swallow-or-miss* clause, and a **disjoint** piece is its harmless branch:
124	`forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` accepts it, and
125	`forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected` (`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:128`) already
126	produces the disjunction for a connected support.  The `∀ j, supp ⊆ pieces j` shape of
127	`forall_noLeak_of_forall_supportLocus_subset` (`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarTube.lean:142`) is a
128	convenience wrapper, and it is the wrapper — not the interface — that is degenerate on a cover
129	with two disjoint pieces.  This paragraph replaces a guard theorem that audited the wrapper and
130	inferred a limit on the assembler; the inference was wrong and the theorem is withdrawn.
131	-/

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard

/-!
# The fibre criterion at the RESTRICTED chart, and the `V`-coupling to coverage

`Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` reduces `IsChartUniv` — antecedent 1 of
`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` — to `IsChartLocusFibre`.  **That reduction passes through the
unrestricted certificate, which the project's headers assert to be false**, and this file is
the repair.

## The defect, measured

`IsChartLocusFibre` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:166`) asks for a
`ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart …) g` at every test — the datum for the *unrestricted*
chart, with `W` a free structure field.  Nothing pins `W := chartLocus`, although the docstring
there says the `W` field "is already discharged — it is `chartLocus`".  So the open `V` never
enters the hypothesis, and one term gives back the unrestricted certificate:

```
isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some
  : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)
```

That measurement is **not** repeated here: it is landed as
`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` and
`mono_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` in `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean`, together
with `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective` — the criterion's own emptiness guard, finally
instantiated at the Abel chart.  In `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` the restriction to `V` is
applied *after* the unrestricted certificate is in hand, so restricting buys nothing on the way
in.

**The precise status of "false".**  `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` and
`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214` all assert that the Abel chart is not injective (the
linear system `|D|`), and by the guard above that assertion makes `IsChartLocusFibre`
unsatisfiable.  But **no declaration proves the non-injectivity**: the guard takes
`¬ Function.Injective` as a hypothesis.  So `IsChartLocusFibre` is *conditionally* unsatisfiable
— dead if the headers are right, and nobody has shown they are.  This file therefore does not
claim the old route is dead; it claims the old route is gated on a proposition the project
believes false and has never checked, which is reason enough not to build on it.

The criterion itself is **not** at fault: it is stated for an arbitrary morphism of presheaves
and is correct.  What was wrong is the *instantiation* — at `abelSigmaChart` rather than at
`restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) V`.

## What this file provides

* `RestrictedChartFibre` — the same datum demanded at the **restricted** chart, so
  `exists_factor` only has to factor test points *of `V`*.
* `isChartUniv_of_restrictedChartFibre` — it gives `IsChartUniv` at that same `V`, one
  application of the existing criterion, with no unrestricted certificate in between.
* `necessity_of_restrictedChartFibre` — the weakening did not delete the content: the restricted
  datum still forces injectivity of the restricted chart on every test.
* `pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre` — **the `V`-coupled assembly** (inbox `I-0861`):
  per-index restricted fibre data on the `hf` side, and on the coverage side the containment
  hypothesis `hV` of `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.liftPointwiseToOpens`, together give the
  representation.  The two sides are made to share the same `V` by typing.

## Division of labour with the two sibling files landed the same round

`Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean` records why the *old* route must not be used, and
`Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean` supplies the **coverage** half of the `V`-coupling
(`liftPointwiseToOpens`, and the converse `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` showing `hV` is
exactly the gap).  This file supplies the **`hf`** half — the fibre datum at the restricted
chart — and the assembly that consumes both.  Nothing here re-proves either sibling.

## The honest limits, stated rather than left for a reviewer

* **Nothing here produces any input.**  This file replaces a badly-gated route by a
  well-gated one; it discharges no antecedent.  `rep` (divisor representability) is a hypothesis
  throughout, and `IsChartUniv` is not even statable without it.
* **`RestrictedChartFibre` at `V = ⊥` IS inhabited — settled in
  `Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`, and an earlier draft of this section priced it
  wrongly.**  That draft said the `sq` field needs
  `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a₁))` over an empty base, "the triviality of `picEt`
  over the empty scheme: true, a genuinely separate lemma, and absent from the tree", and
  concluded that *no satisfiability witness exists at any `V`*.  **Both the pricing and the
  conclusion were false.**  The error was in the reduction, not the census: the `congr 1` that
  peeled the Σ-component and named `pic0Subgroup` threw away the fact that `pic0SigmaSheaf` is a
  **sheaf**, and a sheaf's value at a scheme covered by the empty sieve is terminal.  So the goal
  is closed by `Sheaf.isTerminalOfBotCover` applied to `Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology`
  (both mathlib) with no fact about `picEt` at all — `restrictedChartFibre_bot`.  The
  `exists_factor` half is free as `I-0861` measured; `sq` is free for a different and cheaper
  reason than that draft supposed.
* **Consequence, and it is the sharp form:** the class is non-empty, so the repaired route is not
  a route to an uninhabitable hypothesis, and the unmeasured-inhabitation risk that `ChartTyping`
  (`I-0779`) and `IsChartLocusFibre` carried does **not** apply here.  What that inhabitant also
  shows is that `IsChartUniv` at `V = ⊥` is free (`isChartUniv_bot`) — antecedent 1 carries no
  content in isolation — while the coverage clause is *refuted* at that same value
  (`not_coverageContainment_bot`), and at the other end `V = ⊤` the prices are swapped: coverage's
  containment becomes free and this datum returns the unrestricted certificate.  So the obligation
  is the *coupling*, and any `V` that works must be a proper intermediate open.
* **What that does NOT establish, since a draft of this file claimed it did** (`I-1012`): the two
  endpoints are **not** a non-vacuity check for the assembly below.  Two *bad* values of `V` are
  two refutations; non-vacuity of the pair needs a `V` where both clauses hold.  Inhabitation of
  the **pair** is still unmeasured at every `V`, and `necessity_of_restrictedChartFibre` is not
  that check either.  Only `RestrictedChartFibre` *alone* is now known inhabited.
* **The relation to the old form IS measured, and an earlier draft mispriced it.**  That draft
  said the transport `IsChartLocusFibre → RestrictedChartFibre` "needs the preimage `r ⁻¹ V`
  pushed forward along `W.ι`, which is real work and buys nothing".  Both halves were wrong
  (`I-0936`): it is `restrictedChartFibre_of_isChartLocusFibre` below, twelve lines, needing only
  `IsOpenImmersion.lift` — and it buys the sharp statement, because its hypothesis is exactly the
  coverage half's `hV`.  The "buys nothing" clause was the worse error: a lane holding the old
  form gets `IsChartUniv` *through the certificate three headers call false*, which is this
  file's whole premise.
-/
